canh-rau-ma-nau-nam.name: Pennywort and Straw Mushroom Soup
canh-rau-ma-nau-nam.description: Fresh pennywort and tender straw mushrooms make a light, gently savory soup for a Vietnamese family meal. Pair it with vegetarian braised or stir-fried dishes.
canh-rau-ma-nau-nam.finished_dish: The broth is clear and gently seasoned, with tender mushrooms and pennywort leaves that are just softened and still green.
canh-rau-ma-nau-nam.serving: Ladle into a serving bowl as soon as the leaves soften. Serve hot with rice and a vegetarian braise or stir-fry.
tips: Rinse the pennywort thoroughly, drain it, and add it only after the broth is simmering.
Cook the leaves briefly so they stay green and do not turn mushy.
Choose seasoning granules labeled vegetarian if keeping the soup meat-free.
suggested_pairings: Vegetarian tofu rolls in wild betel leaves
canh-rau-ma-nau-nam.image_alt: Pennywort and straw mushroom soup in a blue-and-white ceramic bowl. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

ingredients.name: Pennywort
ingredients.notes: Pick through, discard wilted leaves, rinse carefully, and drain.

ingredients.name: Straw mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim dirty ends, rinse briefly, and halve larger mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the shallot.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season lightly, then adjust after the mushrooms cook.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Use a small amount to balance the seasoning.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning granules
ingredients.notes: Choose a product labeled vegetarian.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Unseasoned vegetable stock may be used instead.

ingredients.name: Scallion
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice to finish the soup.

preparation_steps: Pick over the pennywort, discard wilted leaves and tough roots, rinse well, and drain. Cut long stems shorter if needed.
Clean the straw mushrooms and halve larger ones. Peel and mince the shallot; rinse and slice the scallion.
Measure the water, salt, sugar, and vegetarian seasoning; add seasonings gradually.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the shallot until fragrant without browning. Add the mushrooms and stir for about 2 minutes.
Add the water and bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook the mushrooms for about 5 minutes and season.
Add the pennywort and cook for 1–2 minutes, just until tender. Taste, scatter over the scallion, and turn off the heat.
canh-rau-ma-nau-nam.serving_basis: A four-person portion for a Vietnamese family meal.
canh-rau-ma-nau-nam.time_note: About 35 minutes including preparation and cooking; actual time varies with the amount of greens and cookware.
canh-rau-ma-nau-nam.media_alt_text: Pennywort and straw mushroom soup in a blue-and-white ceramic bowl. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

dau-hu-cuon-la-lot-chay.name: Vegetarian Tofu Rolls in Wild Betel Leaves
aliases: Vegetarian Tofu and Tofu-Skin Rolls in Lá Lốt
dau-hu-cuon-la-lot-chay.description: Tofu, tofu skin, and wood ear mushrooms are rolled in fragrant wild betel leaves and lightly pan-seared. The soft, pleasantly chewy filling and aromatic leaves make an easy meat-free dish with rice.
dau-hu-cuon-la-lot-chay.finished_dish: The rolls are lightly browned and fragrant, with a moist tofu-and-mushroom filling that holds together.
dau-hu-cuon-la-lot-chay.serving: Serve hot with vegetarian dipping sauce, steamed rice, or rice noodles.
tips: Drain the tofu and tofu skin well so the filling does not turn watery.
Dry the leaves completely before rolling and keep the filling modest to prevent them from splitting.
Use a thin layer of oil and medium-low heat so the leaves cook through without scorching.
search_terms: vegetarian tofu rolls in wild betel leaves
dau-hu-cuon-la-lot-chay.image_alt: Vegetarian tofu rolls wrapped in glossy wild betel leaves on a ceramic plate. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Blanch briefly, drain, and crumble coarsely.

ingredients.name: Fresh tofu skin
ingredients.notes: Blanch briefly, squeeze dry, and chop.

ingredients.name: Dried wood ear mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Soak until soft, rinse, and mince.

ingredients.name: Wild betel leaves (lá lốt)
ingredients.notes: Choose intact leaves, rinse, and dry completely.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Mince finely for the filling.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Check the label for a vegetarian product.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning granules
ingredients.notes: Season lightly because the sauce is already salty.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Use a little to balance the filling.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For lightly coating the pan or grill.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian dipping sauce
ingredients.notes: Serve separately and adjust to taste.

preparation_steps: Soak the wood ear mushrooms in warm water for about 10 minutes, rinse, remove tough stems, and mince.
Briefly blanch the tofu and tofu skin, let them cool, and gently squeeze out excess water. Coarsely mash the tofu and chop the tofu skin and lemongrass.
Rinse the wild betel leaves and dry them completely. Mix the tofu, tofu skin, mushrooms, lemongrass, vegetarian oyster sauce, sugar, and vegetarian seasoning.
Place a leaf shiny-side down, add a modest amount of filling near the stem, fold the sides, and roll tightly. Secure with a toothpick if needed.
cooking_steps: Warm a nonstick pan over medium-low heat and coat it with a very thin layer of oil.
Place the rolls seam-side down first. Turn gently until the leaves are fragrant, cooked through, and lightly blistered, about 5–7 minutes depending on size.
Transfer to a plate and remove toothpicks if used. Serve hot with vegetarian dipping sauce and rice or noodles.
dau-hu-cuon-la-lot-chay.serving_basis: A four-person portion for a family meal.
dau-hu-cuon-la-lot-chay.time_note: About 45 minutes including mushroom soaking, preparation, rolling, and pan-searing.
keywords: Vegetarian Tofu Rolls in Wild Betel Leaves

ga-nau-pate.name: Vietnamese-Style Chicken Pâté Stew
ga-nau-pate.description: Chicken simmers until tender in a rich pâté sauce with potatoes and carrots. This family-meal variation blends French-influenced pâté with Vietnamese home cooking; Bếp Việt presents it as a weekend change-up, not a traditional regional specialty.
ga-nau-pate.finished_dish: The chicken is tender, the vegetables are just soft, and the pâté sauce is smooth and rich, with a mild sweetness from coconut water.
ga-nau-pate.serving: Ladle into a deep serving bowl, garnish with cilantro, and serve hot with bread or steamed rice.
tips: Brown the chicken and potatoes briefly to help them hold their shape while simmering.
Stir the pâté into the butter and tomato sauce over low heat to keep the sauce smooth.
Add the onion near the end so it softens without disappearing; check the thickest chicken pieces are cooked through.
ga-nau-pate.image_alt: Vietnamese-style chicken pieces simmered in pâté sauce with potatoes and carrots in a ceramic bowl. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

ingredients.name: Chicken
ingredients.notes: Cut into even portions; thighs or bone-in pieces work well.

ingredients.name: Pâté
ingredients.notes: Mash with a little coconut water so it blends smoothly into the sauce.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.notes: Peel, rinse, and cut into serving-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into thick rounds or chunks.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into wedges.

ingredients.name: Fresh coconut water
ingredients.notes: Use as the braising liquid; add water if needed.

ingredients.name: Tomato ketchup
ingredients.notes: Adds gentle tang and color to the sauce.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: Reduce the amount if the pâté is already rich.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For searing the chicken and potatoes.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season lightly; pâté and sauce already contain salt.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Use sparingly or omit.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the chicken and finish the dish.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinse and use as a garnish.

preparation_steps: Rinse the chicken, pat dry, and cut into serving-size pieces. Marinate with salt, sugar, and pepper for about 15 minutes.
Peel and cut the potatoes and carrot into chunks. Cut the onion into wedges; mince the shallot and garlic.
Mash the pâté with a little coconut water until smooth and easy to stir into the sauce. Rinse and drain the cilantro.
cooking_steps: Heat some of the oil and quickly sear the potatoes until the outside firms; set aside. In the same pan, sear the chicken until the surface is lightly browned.
Sauté the shallot and garlic in a pot. Add the mashed pâté, butter, and ketchup; stir over low heat until combined.
Pour in the coconut water, stir, and add the chicken. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for about 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrot and simmer until the chicken is fully cooked and the vegetables are tender. Add the onion near the end, taste after the pâté dissolves, and finish with cilantro.
ga-nau-pate.serving_basis: A four-person portion for a family meal.
ga-nau-pate.time_note: About 60 minutes including preparation, brief marinating, searing, and simmering.
ga-nau-pate.media_alt_text: Vietnamese-style chicken pieces simmered in pâté sauce with potatoes and carrots in a ceramic bowl. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

ca-ho-kho-nghe.name: Cutlassfish Braised with Turmeric
aliases: Vietnamese Cutlassfish Braised with Fresh Turmeric
ca-ho-kho-nghe.description: Cutlassfish is marinated with fresh turmeric, shallot, garlic, and seasonings, then slowly braised until the sauce clings to the fish. Its warm turmeric color and gentle heat suit a Central Vietnamese family meal.
ca-ho-kho-nghe.finished_dish: The fish is cooked through and coated in a golden turmeric braising sauce, with aromatic shallot and a mild chili finish.
ca-ho-kho-nghe.serving: Serve hot from the clay pot with steamed rice and a simple vegetable side.
tips: Pat the fish dry after cleaning so it takes on the marinade instead of releasing excess water.
Keep the braise at a gentle simmer and tilt the pot to baste the fish rather than stirring it.
Check the thickest piece is opaque and separates into flakes before serving.
ca-ho-kho-nghe.image_alt: Golden turmeric-braised cutlassfish in a clay pot with scallion and chili. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

ingredients.name: Cutlassfish
ingredients.notes: Clean and cut into 4–5 cm sections.

ingredients.name: Fresh turmeric
ingredients.notes: Rinse, peel, and pound or mince.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush or slice.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese sand onion (củ nén)
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush; omit if unavailable.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust according to saltiness.

ingredients.name: Oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Adds savory depth; reduce if the fish is small.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the seasoning and braising color.

ingredients.name: Caramel cooking sauce
ingredients.notes: Use a small amount for a golden-brown color.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the garlic and shallot.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add enough to keep the fish from sticking to the bottom.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Deseed or reduce for a milder dish.

ingredients.name: Scallion
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into short lengths.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle over the fish at the end.

preparation_steps: Trim the fins, gills, and innards from the cutlassfish. Rinse away surface slime, cut into sections, pat dry, then rub lightly with salt and a little lime before rinsing again.
Rinse and peel the turmeric. Peel the shallots, garlic, and Vietnamese sand onion; crush or mince them.
Marinate the fish with turmeric, shallot, sand onion, fish sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, caramel sauce, chili, and pepper for about 20 minutes.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a clay pot or heavy-bottomed pan. Sauté the garlic until fragrant without letting it burn; lower or turn off the heat if the pot gets too hot.
Arrange the fish and all the marinade in the pot and add the water. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat, partially cover, and braise for 12–15 minutes.
Tilt the pot gently to baste the fish; do not stir with chopsticks. Check that the thickest piece is opaque and flakes easily, taste the sauce, and add the scallion.
Braise for a few more minutes until the sauce lightly thickens. Turn off the heat, finish with black pepper, and serve hot.
ca-ho-kho-nghe.serving_basis: A four-person portion for a Central Vietnamese family meal.
ca-ho-kho-nghe.time_note: About 50 minutes including cleaning, marinating, and braising.
ca-ho-kho-nghe.media_alt_text: Golden turmeric-braised cutlassfish in a clay pot with scallion and chili. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.
